record.context_brief: Finiteness of endomorphism rings over a number field
record.original_question: Fix a number field K and a positive integer g. Are there only finitely many rings that occur as endomorphism rings of g-dimensional abelian varieties defined over K?

evidence.quote: Let K be a number field and g a positive integer. Then show that the number of distinct endomorphism rings of abelian varieties of dimension g defined over K is finite.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $K$ be a number field and let $g$ be a positive integer. For an abelian variety $A$ of dimension $g$ defined over $K$, let $\operatorname{End}_K(A)$ denote its ring of $K$-rational endomorphisms (a $\mathbb{Z}$-order in a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra). Prove or disprove: as $A$ ranges over all abelian varieties of dimension $g$ defined over $K$, the set of isomorphism classes of rings that arise as $\operatorname{End}_K(A)$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is widely known as Coleman's conjecture on the finiteness of endomorphism rings of abelian varieties of fixed dimension over a fixed number field. It remains open in general; partial results are known (e.g., bounds on p-parts of co-indices, results for specific dimensions, and related uniformity conjectures).

status_evidence.title: On finiteness of endomorphism rings of abelian varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Finiteness result concerning p-exponents of co-indices of endomorphism rings of abelian varieties of fixed dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward the conjecture, indicating it is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On uniformity conjectures for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Coleman's conjecture: for all abelian varieties A of dimension g defined over number fields of degree d, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes among End(A).
status_evidence.claim: Coleman's conjecture remains an open uniformity conjecture.
